lines.text: Number a book's pages, and count every digit.
lines.caption: Number a book's pages, and count every digit.

lines.text: Ninety-nine pages use one hundred eighty-nine digits. That's NOT twice ninety-nine!
lines.caption: Ninety-nine pages use one hundred eighty-nine digits. That's NOT twice ninety-nine!

lines.text: A book's pages are numbered from one. The digits printed are exactly twice the number of pages.
lines.caption: A book's pages are numbered from one. The digits printed are exactly twice the number of pages.

lines.text: How many pages does the book have?
lines.caption: How many pages does the book have?

lines.text: Here's the trick. Pretend every page must print two digits.
lines.caption: Here's the trick. Pretend every page must print two digits.

lines.text: A one-digit page pays only one. So each of those nine pages is one digit short.
lines.caption: A one-digit page pays only one. So each of those nine pages is one digit short.

lines.text: A two-digit page pays exactly two. But a three-digit page pays one extra! We need nine of those.
lines.caption: A two-digit page pays exactly two. But a three-digit page pays one extra! We need nine of those.

lines.text: That's pages one hundred to one hundred eight.
lines.caption: That's pages one hundred to one hundred eight.

lines.text: So the book has one hundred eight pages, choice C!
lines.caption: So the book has one hundred eight pages, choice C!

lines.text: Why only one answer? The full lesson shows two ways, plus every trap.
